The "History of Japan for Boys and Girls," the No. 1 series of its kind, has been loved by elementary and junior high school students as preparation for entrance exams nationwide since its publication in 1981, and now it has been completely renewed!

The new "Shogakukan's History of Japan" is amazing!
1. The most important emphasis is placed on "depicting historical facts"!
The manga is based on historical facts that are considered "accurate" to the best of current knowledge, and does not include any extraneous drama. So you can be sure to obtain accurate information.

2. Easy-to-understand illustrated panels including genealogy charts, character correlations, and maps!
Many illustrated informational panels are included in the manga! You can understand difficult subjects, the flow of history, and human relationships all visually!

This series will help you to prepare for the "Comprehensive History Course" required by the new curriculum guidelines! The Japan of the 21st century in which we are now living can be best understood by looking at the "Modern and Contemporary" period from the Meiji Era onward. 160268.description:
After a traumatic accident that causes her to lose all her memories, Hiro tries to make the most out of her day-to-day life. With frequent visits to the doctor and the rippling effects of the incident, it has been hard for Hiro’s life to resume to normal. Especially when she doesn’t remember what “normal” was like. But her lover, Sana, has been very supportive since day one, reassuring her that the, “past doesn’t matter.” Despite this reassurance, Hiro can’t help but feel like the past does matter. In an attempt to know more about life before, she looks for clues in her photo album. Her supportive lover however, doesn’t want her to find out. What exactly is she hiding from Hiro? Is it better know what life was like before the accident or is it best not to know?
